ALP: Alkaline phosphatase (U/L), an enzyme marker for liver, bone, or intestinal function, elevated in hepatobiliary disease or bone disorders.
ALT: Alanine aminotransferase (U/L), a liver-specific enzyme marker for hepatocellular injury, commonly elevated in hepatitis or drug-induced liver damage.
AST: Aspartate aminotransferase (U/L), an enzyme marker for liver and muscle damage, elevated in hepatic disease, myocardial infarction, or skeletal muscle injury.
Albumin: Serum albumin (g/dL), a protein marker of nutritional status and liver synthetic function, decreased in malnutrition, liver disease, or nephrotic syndrome.
BUN: Blood urea nitrogen (mg/dL), a marker of kidney function and protein metabolism, elevated in renal failure, dehydration, or high protein intake.
Bilirubin: Serum bilirubin (mg/dL), a marker of liver function and hemolysis, elevated in hepatobiliary disease, hemolytic anemia, or Gilbert syndrome.
Cholesterol: Serum total cholesterol (mg/dL), a lipid metabolism marker and cardiovascular risk factor, elevated in hyperlipidemia or hypothyroidism.
Creatinine: Serum creatinine (mg/dL), a critical marker of kidney function reflecting glomerular filtration rate, elevated in acute or chronic renal failure.
DiasABP: Invasive diastolic arterial blood pressure (mmHg), measured via arterial catheter, reflects arterial pressure during cardiac relaxation phase.
FiO2: Fraction of inspired oxygen (%), the percentage of oxygen in inhaled air delivered to the patient, critical parameter for ventilation management.
GCS: Glasgow Coma Scale score (3-15), a standardized neurological assessment tool measuring eye opening, verbal response, and motor response to evaluate consciousness level.
Glucose: Blood glucose (mg/dL), a marker of carbohydrate metabolism and diabetes status, critical for detecting hyperglycemia or hypoglycemia in ICU patients.
HCO3: Serum bicarbonate (mEq/L), a key component of acid-base balance, decreased in metabolic acidosis or increased in metabolic alkalosis.
HCT: Hematocrit (%), the percentage of red blood cells in total blood volume, decreased in anemia or increased in polycythemia or dehydration.
HR: Heart rate (beats per minute), a vital sign reflecting cardiac activity and autonomic function, abnormal in arrhythmias, shock, or fever.
K: Serum potassium (mEq/L), a critical electrolyte for cardiac rhythm, muscle contraction, and nerve function, abnormal levels can cause fatal arrhythmias.
Lactate: Blood lactate (mmol/L), a marker of tissue hypoxia and anaerobic metabolism, elevated in sepsis, shock, or tissue hypoperfusion.
MAP: Invasive mean arterial pressure (mmHg), the average arterial pressure over a cardiac cycle, critical for assessing organ perfusion.
MechVent: Mechanical ventilation status (0/1), indicates whether the patient requires respiratory support via ventilator.
Mg: Serum magnesium (mg/dL), an electrolyte vital for neuromuscular function, cardiac rhythm, and enzyme activity, deficiency can cause arrhythmias and seizures.
NIDiasABP: Non-invasive diastolic arterial blood pressure (mmHg), measured via blood pressure cuff, reflects arterial pressure during cardiac relaxation.
NIMAP: Non-invasive mean arterial pressure (mmHg), calculated from non-invasive blood pressure measurements, indicator of organ perfusion.
NISysABP: Non-invasive systolic arterial blood pressure (mmHg), measured via blood pressure cuff, reflects arterial pressure during cardiac contraction.
Na: Serum sodium (mEq/L), a critical electrolyte for fluid balance, nerve conduction, and muscle function, abnormal in dehydration or SIADH.
PaCO2: Partial pressure of carbon dioxide in arterial blood (mmHg), reflects respiratory acid-base balance and ventilation adequacy.
PaO2: Partial pressure of oxygen in arterial blood (mmHg), a key indicator of oxygenation status and pulmonary gas exchange efficiency.
Platelets: Platelet count (cells/mm³), a marker of blood clotting ability, decreased in thrombocytopenia or increased in reactive thrombocytosis.
RespRate: Respiratory rate (breaths per minute), a vital sign reflecting pulmonary function and respiratory drive, abnormal in respiratory distress or failure.
SaO2: Arterial oxygen saturation (%), the percentage of hemoglobin bound to oxygen in arterial blood, critical for assessing oxygenation status.
SysABP: Invasive systolic arterial blood pressure (mmHg), measured via arterial catheter, reflects arterial pressure during cardiac contraction.
Temp: Body temperature (°C or °F), a vital sign reflecting thermoregulation, elevated in infection, inflammation, or hyperthermia.
TroponinI: Troponin I (ng/mL), a highly specific cardiac biomarker for myocardial injury, critical for diagnosing acute myocardial infarction.
TroponinT: Troponin T (ng/mL), a highly specific cardiac biomarker for myocardial injury, used to diagnose acute myocardial infarction and assess heart muscle damage.
Urine: Urine output (mL/hour or mL/day), an indicator of renal function and hydration status, decreased in acute kidney injury or hypovolemia.
WBC: White blood cell count (cells/mm³), a marker of immune response and infection, elevated in bacterial infection or leukemia, decreased in immunosuppression.
pH: Blood pH value (7.35-7.45 normal range), an indicator of acid-base balance status, abnormal in respiratory or metabolic acidosis/alkalosis.
